dialogue.origin: ■おはようございます。
dialogue.content: Good morning.

dialogue.origin: おはようございます。宜しくお願い致します。
dialogue.content: Good morning. I look forward to working with you.

dialogue.origin: はじめてもよろしいでしょうか？
dialogue.content: Shall we begin?

dialogue.origin: ■よろしくお願いします。始めて大丈夫です。
dialogue.content: Yes, please. It's fine to start.

dialogue.origin: ・・・ロールプレイスタート
dialogue.content: ... Beginning the role-play.

dialogue.origin: こんにちは。相談員です。
dialogue.content: Hello. I'm the counselor.

dialogue.origin: こんにちは。
dialogue.content: Hello.

dialogue.origin: 今日はどのようなご相談でしょうか。
dialogue.content: What can I help you with today?

dialogue.origin: 塾のテストでカンニングしちゃったんです。それは悪い事だと思っているんですが、お母さんにバレたらもう生きていけない。
dialogue.content: I cheated on a test at my cram school. I know it was wrong, but if my mom finds out, I feel like I can't go on living.

dialogue.origin: うんうん。そうなのね。
dialogue.content: Mm-hm. I see.

dialogue.origin: お母さんはとにかく1番じゃなきゃダメって…
dialogue.content: My mom says I absolutely have to be number one...

dialogue.origin: ああ、そうなんだね。
dialogue.content: Oh, I see.

dialogue.origin: 1番取ったら取ったで、クラスが下だからねとか言うし。暗記が苦手で、もう精神的にしんどいです。
dialogue.content: Even when I do get first place, she says things like, 'It's only because it's a lower-level class.' I'm bad at memorizing, and it's so mentally exhausting.

dialogue.origin: 一番とってもそう言われてしまうのね。それは、辛いよね。
dialogue.content: So even when you come in first, she still says that. That must be really hard.

dialogue.origin: 勉強は正直言って得意じゃない、得意じゃないから塾に行かせてもらえてどうにか頑張ってるけど、お母さんが厳しくてつらいです。
dialogue.content: To be honest, I'm not good at studying. I'm trying my best since I get to go to cram school, but my mom is so strict, and it's painful.

dialogue.origin: うんうん。
dialogue.content: Mm-hm.

dialogue.origin: お母さん厳しいのね。つらいのね。
dialogue.content: Your mom is strict. That must be painful.

dialogue.origin: お母さんは、塾のお金も無駄だって怒るんです。
dialogue.content: My mom gets angry and says the cram school fees are a waste of money.

dialogue.origin: ああ、そう言われちゃうのね。悲しいね。
dialogue.content: Oh, she says that to you. That’s hurtful.

dialogue.origin: 私がバカなのがいけないって分かってるんだけど、もうホントに生きてけない。
dialogue.content: I know it's my fault for being stupid, but I really feel like I can't go on living.

dialogue.origin: でも、クラスで１番取れるように頑張れるんだよね。
dialogue.content: But you're able to work hard enough to get first place in your class, right?

dialogue.origin: 1番っていっても最下位クラスだし。もうこれ以上頑張れないから、カンニングしちゃった。
dialogue.content: Even though it's first place, it's in the lowest-level class. I couldn't try any harder, so I ended up cheating.

dialogue.origin: しかも、たった1度だけだったし、まぐれだった。
dialogue.content: Besides, it was just once, and it was a fluke.

dialogue.origin: そうなんだ・・・カンニング、一度だけしちゃったの？まぐれって？
dialogue.content: I see... You cheated just once? What do you mean by 'a fluke'?

dialogue.origin: 三者面談が怖すぎ。
dialogue.content: I'm terrified of the parent-teacher conference.

dialogue.origin: 1度だけってのは1番が。
dialogue.content: Getting first place was the one-time thing.

dialogue.origin: もう踏切いく。
dialogue.content: I'm just going to go to the railroad crossing.

dialogue.origin: 塾の前が踏切だし。
dialogue.content: There's a railroad crossing in front of the cram school.

dialogue.origin: 今は、塾にいるの？
dialogue.content: Are you at the cram school right now?

dialogue.origin: 塾はこれから。
dialogue.content: Cram school is later.

dialogue.origin: そうなのね。　じゃ、今はおうちにひとり？
dialogue.content: I see. So, are you home alone right now?

dialogue.origin: お母さんもいるけど、夕飯食べてから塾。
dialogue.content: My mom is here too, but I'll go to cram school after dinner.

dialogue.origin: ああ、そうなんだね。まだ、このまま話続けていても大丈夫？
dialogue.content: Oh, I see. Is it okay if we continue talking for a little longer?

dialogue.origin: ホントに三者面談怖い、怖すぎてもうダメ。
dialogue.content: I'm really scared of the parent-teacher conference; it's so scary I can't handle it.

dialogue.origin: 三者面談はいつなの？
dialogue.content: When is the parent-teacher conference?

dialogue.origin: 今週の土曜日
dialogue.content: This Saturday.

dialogue.origin: ああそうなんだ。それで心配で、今日相談に来てくれたのね。今は３年生？
dialogue.content: I see. So you were worried about that, and that's why you came to talk today. Are you in your third year?

dialogue.origin: もう考えただけで吐きそう。
dialogue.content: Just thinking about it makes me feel like throwing up.

dialogue.origin: 今は1年生。
dialogue.content: I'm in my first year now.

dialogue.origin: 高校？
dialogue.content: High school?

dialogue.origin: もうどうしていいか分かんない。
dialogue.content: I don't know what to do anymore.

dialogue.origin: 中学
dialogue.content: Junior high.

dialogue.origin: ありがとう。中一ね。ちょっと、深呼吸してみてもらえるかな。
dialogue.content: Thank you. First year of junior high, then. Could you try taking a deep breath for me?

dialogue.origin: うん
dialogue.content: Okay.

dialogue.origin: 中一ということは、高校受験まで、まだ時間があるけど。もうそんなに、塾で頑張っているのね。
dialogue.content: Being in your first year of junior high means you still have time before high school entrance exams. You're already working so hard at cram school.

dialogue.origin: バレたらどうしよう、怖い。
dialogue.content: What if they find out? I'm scared.

dialogue.origin: 学校の勉強にもついていけないし。
dialogue.content: I can't keep up with my schoolwork either.

dialogue.origin: 怖い。そうなのね。
dialogue.content: You're scared. I understand.

dialogue.origin: 学校の勉強って、大変だよね。小学校のころと、どういうところが違うと思う？
dialogue.content: Schoolwork can be tough. What do you think is different from elementary school?

dialogue.origin: 進むのが早くて。元々が分かんないから難しい。
dialogue.content: It goes so fast, and because I didn't understand the basics to begin with, it's hard.

dialogue.origin: 暗記もダメ。だからテストがきつい。
dialogue.content: I'm bad at memorizing, too. That's why tests are so tough.

dialogue.origin: でも、点数取らないと怒られる。
dialogue.content: But if I don't get good scores, I get yelled at.

dialogue.origin: うんうん。そうなんだ。はやいんだ。
dialogue.content: I see. It's fast-paced.

dialogue.origin: どんどんついていけなくなる。
dialogue.content: I'm falling further and further behind.

dialogue.origin: やってもやっても。
dialogue.content: No matter how much I try.

dialogue.origin: 焦る気持ちなのかな？点数取らないと怒るのは、お母さんだけ？
dialogue.content: Does that make you feel anxious? Is your mom the only one who gets angry if you don't get good scores?

dialogue.origin: 頭に入らない。
dialogue.content: It just doesn't sink in.

dialogue.origin: そうなのね。小学校の頃は、勉強どうだったの？
dialogue.content: I see. How was studying for you in elementary school?

dialogue.origin: あんまり。
dialogue.content: Not great.

dialogue.origin: お母さんしかいないから、お母さんだけ怒る。
dialogue.content: It's just my mom, so she's the only one who gets angry.

dialogue.origin: 土曜日が怖い、もう死にたい。
dialogue.content: I'm scared of Saturday. I just want to die.

dialogue.origin: うんうん。カンニングしたことがバレるかもしれないから？
dialogue.content: Mm-hm. Is it because you're afraid they might find out you cheated?

dialogue.origin: お母さん、絶対に怒る。
dialogue.content: My mom will definitely get angry.

dialogue.origin: うん、バレたら大変。成績のこと自体も怒るだろうけど、もっと怒る。
dialogue.content: Yes, it'll be a disaster if she finds out. She'll be angry about my grades anyway, but she'll be even angrier about this.

dialogue.origin: でも、今日ここに相談に来てくれたのは、カンニングが悪いことだって感じているからだよね。
dialogue.content: But the reason you came to talk to me today is because you feel that cheating is wrong, right?

dialogue.origin: 悪かったのは悪かった思う。でも言い訳になるけど、もうどうしようもなかった。
dialogue.content: I know it was wrong. This is going to sound like an excuse, but I felt like I had no other choice.

dialogue.origin: うんうん。そうなのね。話してくれて、じんじんと気持ちが伝わってきたよ。
dialogue.content: Mm-hm, I see. As you're talking, I can really feel what you're going through.

dialogue.origin: でも、やっぱり悪いことだよね。
dialogue.content: But it was still wrong, right?

dialogue.origin: そう思うよね。
dialogue.content: You think so too, right?

dialogue.origin: う～ん。それは悪いことかもしれないけど。でも、他にも悪いことってあるとおもうんだけどなぁ。
dialogue.content: Hmm. It might be a bad thing. But I think there are other things that are bad, too.

dialogue.origin: 犯罪まではいかないんだろうけど、お母さんにとってはそれくらい怒ると思う。
dialogue.content: It's probably not a crime, but I think my mom will get as angry as if it were.

dialogue.origin: するどい分析！
dialogue.content: That's a sharp analysis!

dialogue.origin: どうしたらいいのか分からない。
dialogue.content: I don't know what to do.

dialogue.origin: 犯罪ではないけど、お母さんにとっては大変なことだと思っているんだね。
dialogue.content: So while it's not a crime, you feel that for your mom, it's a very big deal.

dialogue.origin: そう。
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: 勉強って　誰のためにするんだろう・・・？
dialogue.content: Who do you think studying is for...?

dialogue.origin: って考えたことあるかな？
dialogue.content: Have you ever thought about that?

dialogue.origin: 勉強できないと仕事にもつけないから、自分ため？
dialogue.content: If you can't study, you can't get a job, so... for myself?

dialogue.origin: 自分のため。そうだよね。
dialogue.content: For yourself. That's right.

dialogue.origin: でも、お母さんに怒られるのは嫌、怖い。
dialogue.content: But I hate getting yelled at by my mom; it's scary.

dialogue.origin: 自分も、子供がこんなに勉強出来なかったら嫌だろうなって思うよね。
dialogue.content: I think if I had a child who was this bad at studying, I'd hate it too.

dialogue.origin: 思うよね → 思う
dialogue.content: I think I would.

dialogue.origin: お母さんの顔見るのもつらい。
dialogue.content: It's painful even to look at my mom's face.

dialogue.origin: そう思うんだ。自分が大人になって子どもが生まれたら、そう思うのね。
dialogue.content: So that's what you think. That if you became an adult and had a child, you would feel that way.

dialogue.origin: そう思いそう。
dialogue.content: I probably would.

dialogue.origin: 中卒でなんか仕事ないだろうし。
dialogue.content: There probably aren't any jobs for someone who only graduated from junior high.

dialogue.origin: 将来、どんな仕事につきたいと考えているの？
dialogue.content: What kind of job do you hope to have in the future?

dialogue.origin: ない。
dialogue.content: None.

dialogue.origin: そうなのね。ねえ、お母さん、怖いって、口だけ？
dialogue.content: I see. Hey, when you say your mom is scary, is it just words?

dialogue.origin: 暴力はないけど、否定されるのがつらい。
dialogue.content: There's no violence, but being invalidated is painful.

dialogue.origin: もうそろそろ塾に行かなきゃ。死んだら三者面談受けなくて済む。
dialogue.content: I have to go to cram school soon. If I die, I won't have to go to the parent-teacher conference.

dialogue.origin: ごめんね。時間だよね。三者面談で、勉強がんばっていることを担任の先生に伝えられる？
dialogue.content: I'm sorry. It's about time, isn't it? At the parent-teacher conference, do you think you can tell your homeroom teacher that you're trying your best with your studies?

dialogue.origin: カンニングしたやつなんか、信じてもらえなさそう。
dialogue.content: They probably wouldn't believe someone who cheated.

dialogue.origin: 三者面談は、お母さんが切れてまくし立てそう。
dialogue.content: At the conference, my mom will probably snap and rant.

dialogue.origin: あー、やだ。
dialogue.content: Ugh, I hate it.

dialogue.origin: そう思うんだ。お母さんが切れると、先生もお話が進められなくなるから、三者面談の前に、先生と二人でお話できないかな？
dialogue.content: You think so. If your mom snaps, the teacher won't be able to proceed with the conversation, so maybe you could talk to the teacher alone before the conference?

dialogue.origin: 今日、タイミングが合えば話したい。でも、話せるかな？、
dialogue.content: I want to talk to them today if I get a chance. But I wonder if I can...

dialogue.origin: うんうん。タイミング、ちょっと頑張って自分で作ってみようよ。カンニングのことは、自分から言うかどうか、お話の流れの中で言ってもいいと思おう。
dialogue.content: Mm-hm. Let's try to make an opportunity for yourself. As for the cheating, you can decide whether or not to bring it up, and just know it's okay to mention it if it comes up naturally in the conversation.

dialogue.origin: カンニングは先生たちはみんな知ってると思う。なんて言ったらいい？
dialogue.content: I think all the teachers know about the cheating. What should I say?

dialogue.origin: ああそうなんだ。それならば、カンニングしちゃったことは悪かった。と正直に受け止める姿勢をあらわして、
dialogue.content: Oh, I see. In that case, show that you honestly accept that cheating was wrong, and then...

dialogue.origin: これから、そんなことをしたい気持ちにならないように、勉強をやりたい　という気持ち、意思を話してみることできるかな？
dialogue.content: ...you can talk about your desire and intention to study so you won’t feel like doing something like that again. Do you think you can do that?

dialogue.origin: 先生に？
dialogue.content: To the teacher?

dialogue.origin: そう、先生に。あなたが、前向きに先生に相談すれば、先生は受け止めてくれると思うよ。
dialogue.content: Yes, to the teacher. If you consult with the teacher with a positive attitude, I think they will be understanding.

dialogue.origin: お母さんに言わないでって言ったらダメ？
dialogue.content: Would it be bad to ask them not to tell my mom?

dialogue.origin: もちろん！　いいよ。はっきりと、先生にそう言っていいと思うの。頑張るあなたを、先生は味方になってくれるよ。先生は大人だから、三者面談の時にも、上手に三人の会話を進めてくださると思うのよ。
dialogue.content: Of course not! It's fine. I think you should say that clearly to the teacher. The teacher will be on your side, supporting you as you try your best. They're an adult, so I'm sure they'll be able to guide the three-way conversation skillfully during the conference.

dialogue.origin: うん、言ってみる。ありがとうございました。
dialogue.content: Okay, I'll try saying it. Thank you very much.

dialogue.origin: よかった。言ってみようね。また、よかったら来週ここにお話しに来てくれるかな？
dialogue.content: That's great. Let's give it a try. If you'd like, could you come back here to talk again next week?

dialogue.origin: はい。
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: 思いっきり　わたしも応援していていい？
dialogue.content: Is it okay if I cheer you on with all my might, too?

dialogue.origin: はい。
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: ドキドキするけど、言ってみます。
dialogue.content: I'm nervous, but I'll try to say it.

dialogue.origin: では、夕食してから塾、気を付けていってらっしゃい。
dialogue.content: Okay then, have dinner and then be careful on your way to cram school.

dialogue.origin: ありがとうございました。
dialogue.content: Thank you very much.

dialogue.origin: では、これで終了させていただきます。Lineの記録は心配だったら消去してくださいね。
dialogue.content: Then, we'll end the session here. If you're worried about the Line chat history, please feel free to delete it.

dialogue.origin: ・・・　ロールプレイ終了
dialogue.content: ... End of role-play.

dialogue.origin: 本日のクライアント役、どうもありがとうございました。
dialogue.content: Thank you very much for playing the client role today.

dialogue.origin: こちらこそ有り難うございました。
dialogue.content: Thank you as well.

dialogue.origin: では、失礼いたします。m(.＿.)m
dialogue.content: Well then, goodbye. m(.＿.)m

dialogue.origin: 失礼します。
dialogue.content: Goodbye.

topic.sub: 母親とのコミュニケーション問題
